core.title: Give every component URN a valid layer value
core.given: A component exists or is being declared, identified by a component URN
core.when: The planner writes, edits or reviews that component URN
core.then: The component URN contains a valid layer value — exactly one value from the profile's allowed layer-role set, spelled exactly as listed there.
prefer: Put the layer in the component URN's layer segment, using one value spelled exactly as in the allowed layer-role set; where the layer segment sits in the URN is a property of the stack's component URN shape, not an additional constraint of this rule.
For reference, each layer role has a typical responsibilities profile (typical operations, consumes, produces) recorded in the profile; consult it when choosing a layer.
If a component spans layers, split it into one component per layer, each with its own URN carrying that single layer value.
avoid: Component URNs with no layer value.
Invented or synonym layer values outside the allowed layer-role set.
Assigning one component to more than one architectural layer (a component belongs to exactly one layer).
core.why: Pinning each component to exactly one layer keeps the layered architecture honest and lets the URN's layer segment be trusted as the single source of truth for where a component lives.
evidence: Each component is assigned to exactly one architectural layer.
Each component URN contains a valid layer value from the profile's allowed layer-role set.
The chosen layer is consistent with that layer role's typical responsibilities profile.
verification: Check: each component URN contains exactly one layer value from the profile's allowed layer-role set, spelled exactly as listed; any other value (invented or synonym) is a violation, and a URN with no layer value is a violation.

The position of the layer segment in the component URN is stack-shape data: the check validates the presence and exact value of the layer, not a fixed segment position. A position shown in a stack's worked example is descriptive, not a grammar requirement.
Exactly-one-layer membership is a separate check: flag any component described or declared under more than one architectural layer.
Consistency of the chosen layer with that layer's typical responsibilities profile is a review judgment against the profile's reference data; it is not a mechanical value check.

The source convention declares no automated implementation for this rule (implementation type none); verification is by review. A stack may provide a URN parser/validator against the allowed layer set plus a membership observer, but the core obligation does not require one.
Non-component URNs are out of scope for this check: other artifact kinds' URNs carry no layer by design.

values: any artifact declaring component URNs (plan artifacts, acceptance artifacts, specs, docs; not limited to changed or plan-only files)
component URN with a layer value outside the allowed layer-role set
component assigned to more than one layer

fires: The planner declares a new component URN in any plan artifact
The planner edits an existing component URN or its layer value
Any component URN (new or existing, changed or not) has no layer value or uses a value outside the allowed layer-role set
A component is described as belonging to more than one layer
doesNotFire: Non-component URNs (other artifact kinds' URNs) that carry no layer by design
Work that neither declares, changes, nor inspects any component

profileRequirements.meaning: The stack's allowed layer-role values (with their local names); the core's allowed layer set for a component URN is exactly this list.
The stack's local name for the composition-root role, which is one of the allowed layer values (so the neutral role list instantiates to the Bun value set).

The component URN shape: a reusable pattern with only the structural constraints the source supports — colon-separated segments, a leading 'component' segment, and exactly one layer segment carrying a value from the allowed layer set. The layer segment's position is stack-defined and descriptive (final segment in the Bun worked example only); it is not a fixed constraint of this core.
profileRequirements.bunValue: component:<…identity segments…>:<layer> — colon-separated; first segment 'component'; exactly one segment carries the layer value from the allowed set; the layer segment's position is a stack choice (in the Bun worked example it is the final segment — descriptive, not a grammar rule)

profileRequirements.meaning: The concrete planning-artifact kinds that can declare component URNs. The activation scope is unrestricted (any artifact declaring component URNs); these kinds are the planning artifacts within it, mapped from the Bun enumeration.
The concrete acceptance-artifact kinds that can declare component URNs, mapped from the Bun enumeration within the unrestricted any-artifact scope.
Per-layer typical responsibilities (typical operations/methods, consumes, produces) used as reference when choosing a layer and when reviewing layer consistency.
profileRequirements.bunValue: presentation: typical methods render/handleInput/updateDisplay, consumes user interactions & display updates, produces ui events & user actions; application: typical methods execute/coordinate/validate, consumes commands & queries, produces events & responses; domain: typical methods process/calculate/applyRules, consumes domain events, produces domain events & state changes; integration: typical methods fetch/save/publish, consumes external events, produces external calls & persistence operations; assembly: no profile in source.

proposedKeys.meaning: Per-layer typical responsibilities (typical operations/methods, consumes, produces) that guide layer choice and layer-consistency review.
proposedKeys.bunValue: presentation: typical methods render/handleInput/updateDisplay, consumes user interactions & display updates, produces ui events & user actions; application: typical methods execute/coordinate/validate, consumes commands & queries, produces events & responses; domain: typical methods process/calculate/applyRules, consumes domain events, produces domain events & state changes; integration: typical methods fetch/save/publish, consumes external events, produces external calls & persistence operations; assembly: no profile in source.
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: roles.layers lists only the layer roles and their local names; no existing key carries the per-layer responsibility patterns that prefer[1], evidence[2] and the layer-consistency review check reference.

neutralityNotes: The allowed layer set is data, not wording: the core defers to the profile's layer-role list, where Bun's 'assembly' is the composition-root role's local name (roles.composition_root.name). The layer-segment position stays descriptive: bun.json's additions explicitly state the final-segment placement comes from its only compliant example and is not a grammar rule, so core.prefer[0] imposes no fixed position, the urn.component profile value is a reusable shape carrying only supported constraints (colon-separated segments, leading 'component' segment, exactly one layer segment), and the final-segment example itself remains bunOnly realization data. The concrete artifact-kind enumeration is mapped into the profile where roles exist (roles.plan_artifact.kinds: plans, wagons, WMBTs; roles.acceptance_test.kinds: acceptances); 'component specs' and 'docs' have no role in the closed vocabulary and remain bunOnly context, while the activation scope stays unrestricted (any artifact declaring component URNs, not limited to changed or plan-only files). The per-layer typical methods/consumes/produces profiles had no vocabulary key, so roles.layer_profiles is proposed. The rule bundles two checks (URN layer-value validity in then; exactly-one-layer membership in avoid[2]/evidence[0]); both are kept so the core is no weaker, even though bun.json itself proposes splitting the membership half into planner.component.single-layer-membership. Concrete examples (the value "service", the compliant project URN, the wagon/WMBT artifact-kind names) are not repeated in the core; they remain in bun.json, which is delivered as the worked reference example. bun.json's unless is empty, and the core keeps it empty. No stack, runtime, framework, language, package manager, file suffix or path is named in the core.
